title: SonicRoute
tagline: Send each app's audio to the device you choose.
intro: Keep music on your speakers and games or calls on your headset. SonicRoute is a Windows audio utility that lives in the system tray: choose output and input devices for individual apps, control audio with hotkeys, the tray wheel or a panel, and combine routine actions into automation rules.
preview: Interface examples: Quick panel for app volume and routing; theme settings for appearance.

mascotAlt: Click the mascot to open the user guide
downloadIntro: For most Windows x64 users, the Microsoft Store build offers convenient installation and automatic updates. Choose Lite x64 for a single executable, or Legacy x64 if installing .NET 8 is not convenient. The download link above always points to the latest release; Lite and Legacy links below are for {release}, while the Store page shows the version currently available there.
storeRequirement: x64; automatic updates; the available version is shown on the Store
runtimeNote: Lite requires the matching {runtime}. Legacy does not require .NET 8.
steps: Start SonicRoute, find its icon in the Windows notification area (it may be under hidden icons), and double-click it to open the full interface.
Select your preferred output and input devices in Settings.
Click the tray icon to open a panel, or set up your hotkeys. Create automation rules when you want to combine actions.
commandNote: `sr` connects only to an already-running SonicRoute instance; it does not start the app. Before first use, start SonicRoute normally to register the command, then close and reopen your terminal. See the {faq} if device switching does not work as expected.

releaseSummary: Version {version} adds direct default-output selection from the tray, controls for the pinned current app’s volume, mute and routing, mute-all-microphones control, and a tray-wheel pause setting saved across restarts. The default hotkey for system-default volume is Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Wheel, distinct from the default Ctrl+Alt+Wheel hotkey for the current app. Settings toggles have been rearranged and pages now load on demand. The Store page shows the version currently available there. See {history} for earlier changes.

features: **Control the app you're using.** Adjust the current audio app's volume, mute it, or change devices without finding it in a list.
**Assign devices per app.** Use speakers for music, headphones for games, and choose microphones separately.
**Open Settings less often.** Handle common tasks with hotkeys, the tray wheel, and the Quick panel without repeatedly opening Windows Settings.
**Repeat fewer steps.** Combine device switching, volume changes, and program launches in automation rules.
